comments.value: Given that this doesn't even address underlying security issues, giving somebody else on the platform kernel level access to my computer is now a real concern. To increase security of a platform, you decrease what it has access to, it's a simple guideline that is practiced in programming  and IT across the globe, and EAC flies in the face of that fundamental principal. We will start to see whole machine compromises from this (note this also happens with antivirus software a ton. People in security don't run AV, as it's placebo security but actually makes things way less secure. EAC runs on the same principals - placebo but hurting not helping)

" EAC also contains a kernel-level component, which on Windows is installed as a kernel driver. This allows EAC code to run at a very privileged level and inspect essentially any and all parts of the system in order to detect tampering. "
@{5f3a1667c9dbb86d5b647895|full_name}: Their implementation is not kernel level. And they've indicated continued linux support which sure sounds like it will not ever be kernel level.

@{5a9fe9983955314156acc4f7|full_name}: You can't have kernel-level components and support Linux. Since Linux/Steam Deck support is still desired by VRChat, the kernel-level component of EAC just won't be enabled.

EAC as a tool for developers does indeed have the ability to be kernel level. However, this and many other features of EAC are up to the Developer if they want to implement them. This is the same feature-set that prevents some games from working on linux. However, they stated it will continue to work on linux, meaning almost certainly they have opted to NOT implement kernel level features. If this changes I'll be just as up in arms about it, but I've seen no indication that they have any kernel level features implemented or will in the future.

@{58de9f2a88e30448a5f75110|full_name}: How to know for certain, though. I take on windows it will still install the kernel-level features when you install EAC?
I guess just running it on Linux is the only way to be certain...
https://www.easy.ac/en-us/partners/  odds are you have before and still do.

@{6245df8fb4bad813bf989eb1|full_name}: I have actively avoided games with an EAC requirement before. It is the main reason I have never played Apex Legends, for instance.
I have even bought games by mistake on Steam, only to realize they required some anti-cheat and not installed them...
I'd rather play those games on console, so I can separate concerns then.

If the VRC team could reassure me that they do not in fact get kernel-level access, I will probably take a lighter stance on this (I still don't like anti-cheat software in general... but if it at least knows its place, I can tolerate it)

@{5f2a4df969e04460cfc5e29d|full_name}: VRChat is the same VRChat.exe downloaded on Proton or otherwise. They don't compile a new one for Steam Deck, and it works fine on Steam Deck. As you know, Steam Deck is a Linux based operating system. Therefore, there is no kernel level access using EAC.

@{5f2a4df969e04460cfc5e29d|full_name}: It positively installs kernel mode driver.  I could not test any other. Because it died immediately in Sandbox. (https://feedback.vrchat.com/open-beta/p/1212-cannnot-test-eac-on-windows-sandbox)

@{5ec1c001131b9c4e90f00b39|full_name}: Of course...
Makes me wonder how the Linux version works, though, as surely Proton can't install windows kernel mode drivers. It could potentially choose a different code path, if it detects it is running under Proton.
I guess running it in Proton or in a VM (that hides it is a VM) is what the future holds...

VAC Is kernel level btw.
VRC's implementation is supposedly not even kernel but I can't confirm that. Either way, Kernal level is just a fear mongering term.
Everything about your data is in Windows so why would it matter if it works below Windows? The big issue with Valorant’s was that it started with Windows without an option to stop it.
@{5f2a4df969e04460cfc5e29d|full_name}: Steam uses VAC, using the same principles.
@{58c6da1b23f8d63e1401d381|full_name}: Several games already have linux EAC support, the most popular example again being Apex Legends.
@{5f2e0a4e8464150716ffd322|full_name}: VAC is not kernel level, and EAC is (on windows). These are well-known facts, stop spreading misinformation.
@{58de9f2a88e30448a5f75110|full_name}: EAC is kernel level on windows. The Linux version is vastly different than the windows one.
@{5f2e0a4e8464150716ffd322|full_name}: I trust MS at least slightly more than I trust Epic Games. How do I know EAC doesn't give Epic a backdoor when it can't even be analyzed in windows sandbox?
@{5f2a4df969e04460cfc5e29d|full_name}: Me too. I really hate anything EPIC touches. If they don't reverse course I am out.

@{6245df8fb4bad813bf989eb1|full_name}: That one seems less invasive, from what I hear about it (but need more research). More crucially, I at least trust Valve a bit more to be ethical. Frankly VAC would be a better alternative to EAC, at least.
In the end, though, I think the best would be something tailor-made for VRC. Just like PhysBones and avatar dynamics was a much better solution than DB.
@{58c6da1b23f8d63e1401d381|full_name}: I don't trust anything that wants an admin prompt unless it is open source.... some things you can't avoid, but if there are alternatives then use them.
@{62def1715d81e144a78ad6ef|full_name}: I am anti EAC, but VAC does appear to be kernel level as well. https://www.reddit.com/r/VRchat/comments/wc9orp/on_eac_and_misinformation/iicoukq/

@{62df1da1465d5152bc63f961|full_name}: I guess the times are just such that you need a dedicated gaming box, or a VM... *sigh*
I do trust valve a bit more to be ethical... but...
**old man yells at c̵l̵o̵u̵d̵  modern computing**
I really wish the devs could've communicated around this a lot better. I had to go look for sources on the implications of this anti-cheat on my own...
@{62e1af4ac223cf44b711f234|full_name}: "alternatives" =>https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/anti-cheat-toolkitactk-is-better-than-eac

In the end, after some research, I decided I can live with EAC... for now. (although I would be incredibly happy if the devs would consider another solution. I believe one can be found that will both serve their needs better, and is less invasive for users)
Longer-term I am looking into running VRC in a VM or perhaps on Linux/Proton inside a container (since the Linux version of EAC doesn't seem to require kernel level access, it is more easily sandboxed). This, or running it on a dedicated computer is what I would recommend others to do as well.
